title: Sell Podcast Clips with Claude: $500 a Month per Client #Shorts
description:
Podcasters have already done the hardest part by talking; you sell distribution without recording a frame. Claude extracts timestamped clips from transcripts, and CapCut formats them. The catch: automated cut lists can cut speakers mid-sentence, so manual audio verification is required.

1. Upload the full episode transcript into Claude to extract 10 timestamped cut points with high-retention hook titles.
2. Import the timestamps into CapCut, apply auto-subtitles and dynamic b-roll, and export 30 vertical clips.
3. Use Claude to draft tailored cold DMs offering 3 free sample clips to podcast hosts on Instagram and LinkedIn.

Tool used:
- name: Claude Chat Transcript Scanner
- endpoint: Scan this podcast transcript. Find 10 standalone segments under 60 seconds with strong curiosity hooks. Output: start/end timestamps, a viral hook title, and a 1-sentence reason why viewers will watch.
- docs: Claude Prompt Engineering Guide

clips.prompt: The man (my avatar) looks into the camera and talks to the viewer like a confident, friendly business tech explainer, smart and natural, not stiff; he leans one hand on a table or railing next to him, then straightens up and talks with a confident open gesture. Vertical 9:16 medium-wide shot from the knees up, camera about two metres away, his head in the upper third with space above it, both hands and all his gestures fully visible in the frame, static camera, sharp and well lit, wearing a light blue oxford shirt with the sleeves rolled up, in a professional video editing suite with two large monitors showing a colour-graded timeline, soft blue ambient light. His face, skin tone, hairstyle, beard, height and body build stay exactly as in my avatar's reference photos - the same natural average build, never slimmer and never heavier. He says, in clear natural English with a natural, clear Indian English accent, at a brisk, lively pace: "Podcasters pay five hundred dollars a month for this. Claude does most of the work." His lips match every word. He starts speaking in the very first frame, with no pause before the first word, and stops right after the last word. Audio: only his voice - no music, no sound effects. No subtitles, no captions, no text on screen.

look: wearing a light blue oxford shirt with the sleeves rolled up, in a professional video editing suite with two large monitors showing a colour-graded timeline, soft blue ambient light
